articles.title: How the Strategic Air Command Would Go to Nuclear War
articles.description: Washington, D.C., March 13, 2019 - Last month’s posting by Robert S. Hopkins on “How the Strategic Air Command Would Have Gone to Nuclear War” provided incredible detail on SAC procedures during the 1960s. Strategic Air Command veteran Bruce Blair takes the story in to the 1970s, with an extraordinary account, based on personal experience, of how SAC would have carried out its nuclear mission if deterrence failed.

articles.title: Dubious Secrets
articles.description: Every year, the US government classifies millions of secrets in the name of protecting the national security.  Shielding genuinely sensitive information is a critical function, but for decades security experts and a growing number of senior government officials have agreed that the system has serious problems. Overclassification is rampant. Decisions about what to keep secret and what to allow the public to see are notoriously subjective. Occasionally, the same official will reach a different conclusion about the same document. Over the years, the National Security Archive has encountered many instances of documents being withheld by one agency or official, only to be released by another. The sheer quantity of these "dubious secrets" points to the systemic weaknesses within the US government’s classification system. The following postings provide some of the more questionable, even downright silly, classification decisions by the national security bureaucracy.

articles.title: Art Before Power: Jenny Holzer showcase
articles.description: Washington D.C., June 17, 2004 - Noted modern artist Jenny Holzer, whose signature "xenon" film projectors have cast monumental light images of texts and truisms on the sides of buildings and landscapes from Florence to Buenos Aires, features the National Security Archive's declassified documents in her latest exhibition, which opened on June 11 in Bregenz, Austria, through September 5.

articles.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis 50th Anniversary
articles.description: In November 1962, Cuba was preparing to become the first nuclear power in Latin America—at the time when the Kennedy administration thought that the Cuban Missile Crisis was long resolved and the Soviet missiles were out.

articles.title: “Heroic Excavators of Government Secrets”
articles.description: Washington, D.C., December 10, 2025 - Almost 40 years ago, as White House aide Lt. Col. Oliver North was secretly running the Reagan administration’s Iran-Contra operations, he became concerned about the activities of a unique, non-profit research center called the National Security Archive.

articles.title: Freedom of Information at 60
articles.description: Washington, D.C., July 9, 2026 - Sixty years after President Lyndon B. Johnson reluctantly signed the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) into law, Americans enjoy a national transparency treasure in their ability to request, obtain, and analyze the records of their own government. Yet obtaining those records has rarely been slower, more difficult, or more uncertain than it is today.

articles.title: “Worst of the Worst”: ICE and the Case of Chilean Intelligence Operative Armando Fernandez Larios
articles.description: Washington D.C., July 10, 2026 - On October 27, 2025, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents quietly detained Armando Fernandez Larios, a former Chilean secret police operative living in Florida. His incarceration at the Krome Detention Center in Miami remained unknown until he appeared on the Department of Homeland Security’s “worst of the worst” list—one of several Trump administration publicity stunts from January 2026 meant to demonstrate that ICE was rounding up immigrants with actual criminal backgrounds.

articles.title: Inside the Struggle to Dismantle America’s Greenhouse Gas Data
articles.description: Washington, D.C., August 18, 2026 – The fossil fuel industry is trying to weaken methane reporting requirements while simultaneously fighting to preserve the related federal emissions database it relies on for credibility, according to U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) records recently released in response to a freedom of information request.

articles.title: Transforming the Mission: The Soviet Military’s Reorientation to a Defensive Posture in Europe
articles.description: Washington, D.C., August 31, 2026 - The “fundamental reevaluation” that took place in the Kremlin under General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev not only encompassed the political, ideological, and economic spheres but also included fundamental changes in military doctrine, according to declassified U.S.

articles.title: “All Roads Lead Through China”: The Clinton Administration, Climate Diplomacy, and China’s Environmental Awakening
articles.description: Washington, D.C., September 17, 2026 - As U.S. officials prepared for the landmark 1997 Conference of Parties (COP) climate negotiations in Kyoto, Japan, they increasingly recognized a simple reality: no meaningful solution to climate change or environmental stewardship would be possible without China, according to declassified documents published today by the National Security Archive.

articles.title: The September 11th Sourcebooks
articles.description: The horrific September 11th terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon brought all of us here at the Archive feelings of rage at the hijackers, grief for the thousands who were murdered, and also determination that we will contribute to finding the best ways for America to respond. The Archive's mission is to put on the record the primary source documentation that can enrich the policy debate, improve journalism, educate policymakers, and ensure that we don't reinvent the wheel or repeat the mistakes of the past.

articles.title: The Letelier-Moffitt Case at 50: The Verdict of History on Pinochet’s Role
articles.description: Washington, D.C., September 21, 2026 - As part of a “major case” investigation into the role of General Augusto Pinochet in an act of terrorism in Washington, D.C., the FBI interviewed former secretary of state Henry Kissinger, according to declassified FBI documents posted today by the National Security Archive. In a meeting with FBI agents on May 25, 2000, in New York, Kissinger related a private meeting he had with General Pinochet in Santiago, Chile, just three months before the assassination, according to a newly disclosed FBI summary of the interview.

articles.title: The CIA Station in Mexico: The Last JFK Assassination Records Secrets
articles.description: Washington, D.C., October 1, 2026 - The CIA continues to keep secret major substantive portions of an internal accounting of its activities in Mexico, including information on covert operations targeting student groups in the days leading up to the massacre at Tlatelolco 58 years ago this week on October 2, 1968.

articles.title: Cubana Flight 455: An Act of Aviation Terrorism 50 Years Later
articles.description: Washington, D.C., October 8, 2026 - Fifty years ago this week, a small bomb of plastic explosives hidden inside a tube of Colgate toothpaste destroyed a civilian Cuban airliner off the coast of Barbados. The mid-air terrorist attack on Cubana flight 455 killed everyone on board, including the entire Cuban national fencing team returning with gold medals from a Panamerican competition.

articles.title: Effective FOIA Requesting for Everyone
articles.description: Government records are fundamental to understanding official policies and the decision-making processes of our leaders. They can be vital resources for a journalist following a breaking news story about government misconduct, a military veteran’s family seeking information about benefits, or a student writing a history paper. Government documents provide first-hand, real-time accounts of events as they unfolded, generally without the editorial filter that characterizes secondary sources like books and news articles.

articles.title: How to File a FOIA Request
articles.description: While Congress passed the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) to increase government accountability and transparency, the FOIA process may seem to further mystify government relations. Many agree that the anatomy of the FOIA is actually more art than science.

articles.title: FOIA Legislative History
articles.description: 1966 Passage The FOIA was enacted in 1966 despite the opposition of President Johnson to the legislation.  Prior to enactment, there were several years of congressional hearings about the need for a disclosure law.   The FOIA went into effect in 1967.  To learn more about the enactment of the FOIA, click here. articles.title: Virtual Reading Room
articles.description: Browse and search through thousands of declassified primary-source materials collected by The National Security Archive.

articles.title: Vietnam Project
articles.description: In the mid-1990s the National Security Archive teamed up with Brown University’s Thomas J. Watson Institute for a conference on "Missed Opportunities in the Vietnam War." Creating the briefing books and furnishing historical expertise for that event, which featured key American and North Vietnamese former officials including Robert McNamara and Nguyen Co Thach, led to the launch of the Vietnam Project. The project compiled two extensive sets of Vietnam-era documents as part of the Digital National Security Archive, many of them published for the first time.

articles.title: The Torture Archive
articles.description: The Torture Archive, an online repository of more than 16,000 documents, chronicles United States government policy on the detention and interrogation of individuals in the “global war on terror” since September 11, 2001.

articles.title: Southern Cone Documentation Project
articles.description: Working with partners in Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay, the Southern Cone Documentation Project aims to support the effort for truth and justice and to address human rights violations committed by military regimes in the region in the 1970s and 1980s. Using U.S. declassified documents and records from regional secret services, project Director Carlos Osorio has introduced critical evidence in multiple judicial proceedings including trials featuring Operation Condor and Operation Mexico (both in Argentina), and against Uruguayan former President Juan Maria Bordaberry.

articles.title: Openness in Russia and Eastern Europe
The Nunn-Lugar Project
articles.description: A documentation and critical oral history project on 20 years of the arms race in reverse, seeking lessons learned and unlearned for future cooperation on denuclearization.

articles.title: The Nuclear Vault
articles.description: Since the founding of the National Security Archive, nuclear crises, nuclear proliferation, and the role of nuclear weapons in U.S. policy have been central to its FOIA requesting. The overwhelming importance of the problem of nuclear weapons has posed an existential threat since the early years of the Cold War and has made this an essential focus.

articles.title: Mexico Project
articles.description: Since 1994, and intensively since 2000, the National Security Archive's Mexico Project has sought to identify and obtain the release of documents from secret government archives on United States and Mexico since 1960, and to disseminate those records through publications, conferences and the Archive's Web site. In order to obtain the declassified documents, we use the Freedom of Information Act to compel U.S. agencies such as the State Department, CIA, Pentagon, Treasury Department and Justice Department to review and release records relevant to the project.

articles.title: Korea Project
articles.description: The project on U.S. policies regarding the two Koreas produced two major collections of declassified documents covering the years from 1969 to 2010. These documents open a window on U.S. policies regarding a critical national security challenge born of the Cold War. The primary focus of these sets was on U.S. management of its alliance with South Korea and efforts to deal with North Korea’s challenges to security and stability on the Korean Peninsula, most importantly Pyongyang’s nuclear ambitions.

articles.title: The U.S.-Japan Project:
articles.description: The Archive’s project on U.S.-Japan relations began in 1993 and worked to  secure declassification of key documents that shed light on U.S. policies toward and relations with Japan between the Kennedy and Clinton administrations. The project focused on diplomatic, security and economic relations between the two countries and produced three document sets, with the last set published in 2012.

articles.title: The Iraq Project
articles.description: The National Security Archive’s Iraq Project began in the early 1990s and has worked for more than two decades to secure and curate historically significant documents regarding U.S. relations with Iraq, with a specific emphasis on “Iraqgate” and the 2003 Iraq War.

articles.title: Iran-U.S. Relations
articles.description: The Iran-U.S. Relations Project promotes the multinational, multi-archival exploration of “hot button” issues in the two countries’ complex relationship spanning more than 70 years. Our documentary holdings, from Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests and archival spelunking on location in Tehran, Baku, Moscow, London and elsewhere, range from a collection of the published, shredded files taken from the U.S. Embassy in Tehran in 1979, to key episodes such as the 1946 Azerbaijan crisis, the 1953 coup, and the 1980s Iran-Iraq War, all the way to the JCPOA.

articles.title: Intelligence Documentation Project
articles.description: The mission of the Intelligence Documentation Project is to expand significantly the public’s understanding of one of the most sensitive areas of U.S. national security policy – the Intelligence Community (IC).  Through extensive use of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), the project has placed in the public domain thousands of previously classified records that describe and contextualize many facets of the IC’s history, organization, structure, mission and operations.

articles.title: Indonesia Documentation Project
articles.description: Since 2002, the National Security Archive's Indonesia / East Timor documentation project has sought to identify and obtain the release of thousands of secret US documents concerning US policy toward Indonesia and East Timor from 1965 to the present.  The work aims to assist East Timorese and Indonesian official and nongovernmental efforts to document and seek accountability for more than three decades of human rights abuses committed during the rule of Indonesian President Suharto (1965-1998), and to contribute to current campaigns in Indonesia for more open government.

articles.title: The Genocide Documentation Project
articles.description: The Genocide Documentation Project launched in January 2013 in partnership with the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum and explores the failures of the international community to prevent or effectively respond to past cases of genocide. Through detailed case studies of Srebrenica, Rwanda, and Darfur, the project examines the role of the international community in these incidents of genocidal violence and helps shape the views of a new generation of policymakers both within the United States and around the world.

articles.title: Colombia Project
articles.description: Promoting access to information and the preservation of the historical record in support of peace, accountability and transitional justice in Colombia.

articles.title: Climate Change Transparency Project
articles.description: The Climate Change Transparency Project focuses on uncovering previously closed and classified documents that illuminate the policy debates and decisions that have guided the United States through more than 40 years of climate change negotiations and global environmental issues. Read more about the project

articles.title: China Documentation Project
articles.description: The China Documentation Project has had as its mission the collection and preservation of declassified records on various topics relating to U.S. government policy toward the People's Republic of China. Archive staff and fellows have filed hundreds of Freedom of Information Act requests and visited numerous presidential libraries in the course of building the collection.

articles.title: The Chile Documentation Project
articles.description: For more than a decade, the Chile Documentation Project set a standard for declassified evidence and impact, becoming a model for responding to challenges and opportunities for truth, justice, and accountability in Peru, Brazil, and Bolivia, where the Archive has also pursued substantive declassification projects. More >>

articles.title: The Afghanistan-Taliban Project
articles.description: The Afghanistan-Taliban project at the National Security Archive has submitted thousands of Freedom of Information Act requests in an effort to contribute evidence to the ongoing public debate on the war, U.S. national security and the evolution of politics and interest in this critical region.

articles.title: Publications
articles.description: One of the National Security Archive's core missions is to disseminate historically valuable and previously unavailable U.S. government documentation to a global audience.
